segments.text: Snow against the window
Bourbon in the glass
Fairbanks in December
Headlights crawling past
Bartender knows better
Than to ask me why
I'm drinking to the woman
I was lucky to survive
We rented half a duplex
By the old Steve's road
With a heater full of thunder
And a roof that bowed with snow
She could kiss me like a promise
Then accused me with her eyes
By midnight every tender word was twisted into knives
I learned to read the weather in the muscles of her face
One minute I was everything, the next I was replaced
Those borderline knots kept moving every wall
I loved her but I couldn't be the answer to it all
So fill it to the frost line. Let the old jukebox complain. I don't want that life back. I just miss it now. And then 40 below and one more round.
Her memory comes sliding when the sun goes down. She was wild as the river when the ice breaks free. That woman was crazy. And she was crazy for me.
i'm glad it's over swear i know that's true no more slam doors no more driving avenue too
i won't call her number i won't go back again but sometimes sometimes i remember when
there were summer nights a creamer's field mosquitoes in our hair she danced beside the
pick up like the whole world wasn't there then jealousy would find us before we made it home
she'd throw my coat into the yard and hide my telephone i tried to hold the center while the
center wouldn't stay tried patience tried forgiveness tried the careful things to say
but love became a checkpoint every breath became a test you can give somebody everything and still
not give them rest now the bottle makes a halo round the places we went wrong and every bad decision
gets a pretty little song fully below and one more round her memory comes sliding when the sun
goes down she was wild as a river when the ice breaks free that woman was crazy and she was
crazy for me i'm glad it's over swear i know that's true no more slam doors no driving avenue
too i won't call her number i won't go back again but sometimes sometimes i remember when
i remember blue light rising over china in the spring
her cheek against my shoulder not demanding anything for one clean little minute we were
quiet we were kind that's the piece the whiskey keeps polishing in my mind but a photograph ain't
shelter and a spark is not a stove i miss the heat between us i don't miss losing hope
40 below this is my last round her memory can visit but it can't move back to town she was
wild as a river i was drowning willingly that woman was trouble and she was tangled up with me
i'm glad it's over and tonight i know it's true no more frozen apologies beneath that fairbanks
moon i turn my phone face down before the old age starts she can keep the northern fire i'm taking
back my hall. Snow against the window, morning coming slow. Here's to what was beautiful and
what I had to let go. I miss the fire sometimes, but I won't mistake it for home. No, I won't
mistake it for home.
You
